Most occasional alcohol bloating clears within **24 to 72 hours** , while chronic irritation or gut changes can take weeks to settle.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnAEBxCJF1xhkVvXdJXIpEfoJJ8J9zGK2h3uifsDxdMSjMOpzyAW5xTWrBW30V_ci-zn9Tv29da3B3rPnX-ZTYs67Vt9FiC0ZwbONauAiNpcbm2WbWTB1tj1Bunl4lGfn6mnCj2EYWmuHWpMYIoiXHCuWeFj1lfU-8-90_D3dUzp6Kcqj5ECRFfZYurfVwO51T4TyqS-Q0WPAAKE9nQo)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXX5FGckXRF3DTRnIMoJcAsiV-sxc86xAEaG6SulkyKcUw1g9IxvKt4iJYpK1ELTUcwzuHxvals8wZuLjxks5rVvR6tV3SnurZae4P6qY_Lxjb1DG2xt2H6VpkdD-ectvCqp8Zd0S2cl7igG2yBSn0fE6khB4OMiQ)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF18xpMfGVuGL-jxsY0CYf4KEJgeAs_lI5u5h9t-e234o4-EqyMIsKTd-6aE6EhoBqNeklpKni4W8__EQjavFiHyy7jUAcxz5WJUfh_gMwHu1AWha7IF3FcL5PWUXPXFxLyRgSvMLJ4LYYCKsGCifrie-9KXavQtyjuFuXv2zC8-lx7wtebfZCo4HHhts)

### Why It Happens

- **Stomach irritation and acid:** Alcohol can inflame the stomach lining (gastritis) and increase stomach acid or reflux.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXdjTCNm88pnP183C5V4jBSQVdjuuSeHPDWOJwuowb_lk_YBskvg2ByDMu-gbgR5wBssl-AZFhxhniLopBcTuu-NnQTSUmseTzfyx1lxIOX02DIDcghEPnmEWzK2i4_nuZPPNw3KUVdHqLPDYLppez)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnAEBxCJF1xhkVvXdJXIpEfoJJ8J9zGK2h3uifsDxdMSjMOpzyAW5xTWrBW30V_ci-zn9Tv29da3B3rPnX-ZTYs67Vt9FiC0ZwbONauAiNpcbm2WbWTB1tj1Bunl4lGfn6mnCj2EYWmuHWpMYIoiXHCuWeFj1lfU-8-90_D3dUzp6Kcqj5ECRFfZYurfVwO51T4TyqS-Q0WPAAKE9nQo)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXIqmcjg2K35wHhO3hQWapewxTpYTC8vWXpRfYIRMim24tiMYTnToo_oA1gh28vp7sgP7o6s1EqEetqSjBKHB3BdasTP4giqFu_82f8f4I4wgJi6cam50nAIvCr4C9D76bA5h7uJpu)
- **Gas and sugar fermentation:** Beer, cider, sparkling wine, and soda mixers introduce carbonation. Sugary mixers and carbs can also ferment in the gut and produce gas.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXIqmcjg2K35wHhO3hQWapewxTpYTC8vWXpRfYIRMim24tiMYTnToo_oA1gh28vp7sgP7o6s1EqEetqSjBKHB3BdasTP4giqFu_82f8f4I4wgJi6cam50nAIvCr4C9D76bA5h7uJpu)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXdjTCNm88pnP183C5V4jBSQVdjuuSeHPDWOJwuowb_lk_YBskvg2ByDMu-gbgR5wBssl-AZFhxhniLopBcTuu-NnQTSUmseTzfyx1lxIOX02DIDcghEPnmEWzK2i4_nuZPPNw3KUVdHqLPDYLppez)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF18xpMfGVuGL-jxsY0CYf4KEJgeAs_lI5u5h9t-e234o4-EqyMIsKTd-6aE6EhoBqNeklpKni4W8__EQjavFiHyy7jUAcxz5WJUfh_gMwHu1AWha7IF3FcL5PWUXPXFxLyRgSvMLJ4LYYCKsGCifrie-9KXavQtyjuFuXv2zC8-lx7wtebfZCo4HHhts)
- **Slower digestion:** Alcohol can slow stomach emptying and alter gut bacteria, leading to trapped gas and fullness.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXTkY3II1AQp-MMmWwvXkaScfbG7nfLqhc9a3Uc8TqU0ll3snS1Smb5BCrQIXOwYXT6TwsN--75PwLZxrCiNQsQezXZqqLU9_2CxAEfSRe-X7pTMDM8C0SL_fa9UBzqyZo-g)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESnAEBxCJF1xhkVvXdJXIpEfoJJ8J9zGK2h3uifsDxdMSjMOpzyAW5xTWrBW30V_ci-zn9Tv29da3B3rPnX-ZTYs67Vt9FiC0ZwbONauAiNpcbm2WbWTB1tj1Bunl4lGfn6mnCj2EYWmuHWpMYIoiXHCuWeFj1lfU-8-90_D3dUzp6Kcqj5ECRFfZYurfVwO51T4TyqS-Q0WPAAKE9nQo)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF18xpMfGVuGL-jxsY0CYf4KEJgeAs_lI5u5h9t-e234o4-EqyMIsKTd-6aE6EhoBqNeklpKni4W8__EQjavFiHyy7jUAcxz5WJUfh_gMwHu1AWha7IF3FcL5PWUXPXFxLyRgSvMLJ4LYYCKsGCifrie-9KXavQtyjuFuXv2zC8-lx7wtebfZCo4HHhts)
- **Fluid shifts:** Alcohol acts as a diuretic, and dehydration or salty bar snacks can cause your body to hold onto water or look puffy.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXcvEKiCsrFcifyRDPTcVwlf4JdqKbKJhrJltmnWEggkoGXllA2MlPSsur3k8zlw16TIhrTrUA9yH6i0eLO9VJ38e4i99vMCvMOeMyD19ejK-UzYd7HkD0RviV8ue2qc4X81O68n_T064)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXlZ-ZzmXHr6g9-FBuOXJa0i3Lh9BTsWk6D8l2ef8PWwovPgtKUVi4_FdxQe2xUQTEYKK0SPbcYrjBOypZsCTwQvE31nHPtVsVSUgANd9soiVRhejFeAR5MTuHEpW1HaWC1MUB7DR_WPfZ0dHW_nxU9bfyGM5HSmSl)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEBxCJF1xLHuquRStErKIA_8RBwuTzAnE-kI3_7dnjnNPsk3ae3VfSArCKPxvHDtIl7RBE8ztJ7yp9sJLHS4DysJVwJDt5FdBACNogBcHhAx2m71kBaVQYWHj23nNbdafMutcPhoxOET52jZUGxvPX-VHuZ8A86N21_98kkmjsKlQcuFIQuU7FQcA)

### Ways to Relieve and Prevent It

- **Drink water:** Sip water alongside drinks and afterward to rehydrate and help digestion.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXX5FGckXRF3DTRnIMoJcAsiV-sxc86xAEaG6SulkyKcUw1g9IxvKt4iJYpK1ELTUcwzuHxvals8wZuLjxks5rVvR6tV3SnurZae4P6qY_Lxjb1DG2xt2H6VpkdD-ectvCqp8Zd0S2cl7igG2yBSn0fE6khB4OMiQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXcvEKiCsrFcifyRDPTcVwlf4JdqKbKJhrJltmnWEggkoGXllA2MlPSsur3k8zlw16TIhrTrUA9yH6i0eLO9VJ38e4i99vMCvMOeMyD19ejK-UzYd7HkD0RviV8ue2qc4X81O68n_T064)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF18xpMfGVuGL-jxsY0CYf4KEJgeAs_lI5u5h9t-e234o4-EqyMIsKTd-6aE6EhoBqNeklpKni4W8__EQjavFiHyy7jUAcxz5WJUfh_gMwHu1AWha7IF3FcL5PWUXPXFxLyRgSvMLJ4LYYCKsGCifrie-9KXavQtyjuFuXv2zC8-lx7wtebfZCo4HHhts)
- **Choose lower-gas drinks:** Still wine or clear spirits with non-carbonated mixers usually cause less gas than beer or fizzy drinks.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF18xpMfGVuGL-jxsY0CYf4KEJgeAs_lI5u5h9t-e234o4-EqyMIsKTd-6aE6EhoBqNeklpKni4W8__EQjavFiHyy7jUAcxz5WJUfh_gMwHu1AWha7IF3FcL5PWUXPXFxLyRgSvMLJ4LYYCKsGCifrie-9KXavQtyjuFuXv2zC8-lx7wtebfZCo4HHhts)
- **Move gently:** A short 10-to-20-minute walk can help move trapped gas and support digestion.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF18xpMfGVuGL-jxsY0CYf4KEJgeAs_lI5u5h9t-e234o4-EqyMIsKTd-6aE6EhoBqNeklpKni4W8__EQjavFiHyy7jUAcxz5WJUfh_gMwHu1AWha7IF3FcL5PWUXPXFxLyRgSvMLJ4LYYCKsGCifrie-9KXavQtyjuFuXv2zC8-lx7wtebfZCo4HHhts)
- **Soothe your stomach:** Herbal teas like ginger or peppermint, or an over-the-counter gas remedy (such as simethicone) or antacid, may ease discomfort.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXdjTCNm88pnP183C5V4jBSQVdjuuSeHPDWOJwuowb_lk_YBskvg2ByDMu-gbgR5wBssl-AZFhxhniLopBcTuu-NnQTSUmseTzfyx1lxIOX02DIDcghEPnmEWzK2i4_nuZPPNw3KUVdHqLPDYLppez)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXIqmcjg2K35wHhO3hQWapewxTpYTC8vWXpRfYIRMim24tiMYTnToo_oA1gh28vp7sgP7o6s1EqEetqSjBKHB3BdasTP4giqFu_82f8f4I4wgJi6cam50nAIvCr4C9D76bA5h7uJpu)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF18xpMfGVuGL-jxsY0CYf4KEJgeAs_lI5u5h9t-e234o4-EqyMIsKTd-6aE6EhoBqNeklpKni4W8__EQjavFiHyy7jUAcxz5WJUfh_gMwHu1AWha7IF3FcL5PWUXPXFxLyRgSvMLJ4LYYCKsGCifrie-9KXavQtyjuFuXv2zC8-lx7wtebfZCo4HHhts)
- **Cut back or take a break:** Reducing how much or how often you drink is the most reliable way to prevent alcohol-related bloating. For more details on causes and recovery steps, see [Healthline](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXcvEKiCsrFcifyRDPTcVwlf4JdqKbKJhrJltmnWEggkoGXllA2MlPSsur3k8zlw16TIhrTrUA9yH6i0eLO9VJ38e4i99vMCvMOeMyD19ejK-UzYd7HkD0RviV8ue2qc4X81O68n_T064) or [Medical News Today](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXIqmcjg2K35wHhO3hQWapewxTpYTC8vWXpRfYIRMim24tiMYTnToo_oA1gh28vp7sgP7o6s1EqEetqSjBKHB3BdasTP4giqFu_82f8f4I4wgJi6cam50nAIvCr4C9D76bA5h7uJpu).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdAHEIkXXdjTCNm88pnP183C5V4jBSQVdjuuSeHPDWOJwuowb_lk_YBskvg2ByDMu-gbgR5wBssl-AZFhxhniLopBcTuu-NnQTSUmseTzfyx1lxIOX02DIDcghEPnmEWzK2i4_nuZPPNw3KUVdHqLPDYLppez)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXcvEKiCsrFcifyRDPTcVwlf4JdqKbKJhrJltmnWEggkoGXllA2MlPSsur3k8zlw16TIhrTrUA9yH6i0eLO9VJ38e4i99vMCvMOeMyD19ejK-UzYd7HkD0RviV8ue2qc4X81O68n_T064)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXIqmcjg2K35wHhO3hQWapewxTpYTC8vWXpRfYIRMim24tiMYTnToo_oA1gh28vp7sgP7o6s1EqEetqSjBKHB3BdasTP4giqFu_82f8f4I4wgJi6cam50nAIvCr4C9D76bA5h7uJpu)

### When to Seek Care
Get medical attention if bloating lasts longer than a few days or keeps coming back. Seek prompt care if you have severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, vomiting blood or dark material, yellowing skin or eyes (jaundice), or fever.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXtwrvKfQ4zCwBdspSUP4pRPRsxc-Yo7AucynLDO05vvivBnphq1F-IC1JqN5Kl6wdY_ZnGzZuzygLhC3tk4h6aSD7b1J-Do33AkdQBa9TS3dnG3s-UUH2eMgZA758DkXQoyJXvEM)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXX5FGckXRF3DTRnIMoJcAsiV-sxc86xAEaG6SulkyKcUw1g9IxvKt4iJYpK1ELTUcwzuHxvals8wZuLjxks5rVvR6tV3SnurZae4P6qY_Lxjb1DG2xt2H6VpkdD-ectvCqp8Zd0S2cl7igG2yBSn0fE6khB4OMiQ)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF18xpMfGVuGL-jxsY0CYf4KEJgeAs_lI5u5h9t-e234o4-EqyMIsKTd-6aE6EhoBqNeklpKni4W8__EQjavFiHyy7jUAcxz5WJUfh_gMwHu1AWha7IF3FcL5PWUXPXFxLyRgSvMLJ4LYYCKsGCifrie-9KXavQtyjuFuXv2zC8-lx7wtebfZCo4HHhts)Are you asking for **yourself** or **someone else** , and is the bloating happening **after a night of drinking**, **regularly** , or **after quitting alcohol** ? Sharing any **other symptoms** (like heartburn, nausea, or pain) can also help me tailor this information.

items.title: Why It Happens
items.text: Stomach irritation and acid: Alcohol can inflame the stomach lining (gastritis) and increase stomach acid or reflux. Gas and sugar fermentation: Beer, cider, sparkling wine, and soda mixers introduce carbonation. Sugary mixers and carbs can also ferment in the gut and produce gas. Slower digestion: Alcohol can slow stomach emptying and alter gut bacteria, leading to trapped gas and fullness. Fluid shifts: Alcohol acts as a diuretic, and dehydration or salty bar snacks can cause your body to hold onto water or look puffy.

items.text: Drink water: Sip water alongside drinks and afterward to rehydrate and help digestion. Choose lower-gas drinks: Still wine or clear spirits with non-carbonated mixers usually cause less gas than beer or fizzy drinks. Move gently: A short 10-to-20-minute walk can help move trapped gas and support digestion. Soothe your stomach: Herbal teas like ginger or peppermint, or an over-the-counter gas remedy (such as simethicone) or antacid, may ease discomfort. Cut back or take a break: Reducing how much or how often you drink is the most reliable way to prevent alcohol-related bloating. For more details on causes and recovery steps, see Healthline or Medical News Today.

items.title: When to Seek Care
items.text: Get medical attention if bloating lasts longer than a few days or keeps coming back. Seek prompt care if you have severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, vomiting blood or dark material, yellowing skin or eyes (jaundice), or fever.
